answer:
The name is built up in three layers, one per feature that touched the face, from the inside out:

1. **`base.outline.bottom`** — the sketch. In your [script.js](lab:open?file=script.js), the base sketch has a rect named `outline`, and its bottom side is the sketch entity `outline.bottom`. Sketch entities are named by their own ids, so this part is stable even if you re-solve the sketch.

2. **`body/side[base.outline.bottom]`** — the extrude named `body`. Each side wall of the extrusion is a `side` face, tagged with the sketch entity it was swept from. So this face is "the wall of `body` that came from the bottom edge of `outline`."

3. **`shell/inner[body/side[base.outline.bottom]]`** — the shell. Shelling offsets each outer wall inward; the new inner wall is an `inner` face of the shell feature, tagged with the face it was derived from — the `body/side…` face above. It inherits that face's whole genealogy, recursively.

So the name reads backwards like a provenance chain: *the inner wall of the shell, which came from the bottom-side wall of the extrude, which was swept from the bottom edge of the sketch's outline*. `why()` confirms it: the chain is `shell/inner[…] ← shell: offset of body/side[…]` and `body/side[…] ← body: swept from sketch entity base.outline.bottom`.

This is why names survive edits: if you change the wall thickness in [param wall](lab:param?name=wall), or fillet the corners later, the same `body/side[base.outline.bottom]` face still exists (possibly split into `#a`/`#b` if another feature cuts it), so selectors like `j.feat('body').sideFaces()` and face queries keep resolving to the same walls. [Open the face](lab:face?name=shell/inner[body/side[base.outline.bottom]]) to see it highlighted.

**What happens at 3 mm:** the [shell feature](lab:node?id=shell) (script.js line 25) fails with *"shell of body1 by 3 mm failed (OpenCascade could not offset the faces)"*, and with it the whole part fails to compile — no body at all.

**Why:** the base extrude has 3 mm fillets on the four vertical corner edges (that's why the box has 19 faces). Shelling offsets the walls *inward* by the wall thickness, so the inner corner radius is roughly `fillet − wall`. At wall = 3 mm the inner corner radius collapses to zero and the offset surface degenerates, so the kernel refuses. At 2.9 mm it still squeaks through with a 0.1 mm knife-edge inner corner — which is why volumes jump disproportionately between 2.8 and 2.9 mm; anything from about 2.9 up is geometrically untenable.

If you genuinely want 3 mm walls, the fix would be to shrink the corner fillet to something like 2 mm (or fillet after shelling at the outer radius), so the inner corner keeps a positive radius. I haven't changed anything — say the word and I'll edit script.js and re-run.
